1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; LLM: large language model; API: application programming interface

  • Identifying error types and choosing a recovery strategy
  • Trace analysis to find failure modes
  • Isolating the origin of a problem: integration layer or model output
  • Evals: success criteria, design principles and grading

2Debugging a Claude Application

Running case

Tidewater's Assistant "Stopped Working"

  • Complaint 1: "No answers at all since this morning"
  • Complaint 2: "Answers are wrong about deductibles for some policies"
  • Complaint 3: "Some replies are cut off"

Step 1: classify the failure

Symptom Likely origin Recovery
4xx (400, 401, 403, 404, 413) Integration: bad request, key, permission, size Fix the request or configuration; retrying unchanged will not help
429 Rate limit Back off, honor retry-after, lower concurrency, spread load
5xx, timeout, overloaded Transient platform condition Retry with exponential backoff and jitter; fall back or queue
stop_reason: max_tokens / cut-off text Output limit Raise max_tokens, ask for shorter output, or continue
JSON fails to parse / schema violation Output format Structured output, defensive parsing, retry with the error
Tool errors Tool or its inputs Fix the tool; return clear is_error results
Plausible but wrong content Model output: prompt, context or data Check the input the model actually saw; grounding, examples, evals
Slow or costly Context bloat, model or effort too high Prune context, cache, route, lower effort

Step 2: use traces

  • Log for every call: request ID, model, parameters, the full prompt actually sent (with sensitive data masked), tool calls and results, usage, stop_reason, latency and the final output.
  • Trace analysis reads these records end to end to see where the chain went wrong: wrong context retrieved, a tool returned bad data, the prompt dropped a rule, or the parser rejected a valid reply.

Step 3: isolate the origin

  • Replay the exact request (same prompt, context and parameters). If the bad output reproduces, the cause is the prompt, context or model behavior; if the request itself was malformed or lost data on the way (a truncated history, a missing document, wrong serialization), the cause is the integration layer.
  • Check what the model actually received: most "model mistakes" turn out to be missing, stale or truncated input.
  • Change one variable at a time and compare.
Exam tip

"Wrong answers" are often wrong or missing input. Look at the logged prompt and tool results before rewriting the prompt or switching models.

Exam tip

Check what the model actually received (the logged prompt and tool results) before changing the prompt or the model.

3Evals

An eval is a repeatable test that measures quality on representative inputs. Without evals you cannot tell whether a prompt, model or setting change helped or hurt.

Part What to know
Success criteria Define them first and make them measurable: task fidelity, consistency, latency, cost, safety
Design principles Task-specific (mirror real inputs, include edge cases), automate where possible, volume over perfect quality (many automatically graded cases beat few hand-graded ones)
Grading Code-based (exact or string match: fastest, most reliable); human (best nuance, slow and costly); LLM-based (fast and scalable for complex judgments: needs a clear rubric, a specific output such as correct or incorrect, optional reasoning, and a reliability check first)
Use Run on every change (prompt, model, tool, config), in CI; track regressions; keep a set of past failures as regression tests

Exam tip

Choose the grading method by need: exact answers → code-based; open-ended quality → LLM-based with a rubric (validated against human judgment); final high-stakes calibration → human review.

4Exam Q&A

S1Requests suddenly return HTTP 401. What should the team do?

  • ACheck the key or credentials; retrying unchanged will not help
  • BRaise max_tokens
  • CSwitch models
  • DRetry with exponential backoff until the request works
Show the answer

Answer: A. 4xx authentication errors need a configuration fix, not retries.

S2During peak hours some calls return 429 with retry-after. What is the best response?

  • ABack off for the indicated time and reduce concurrency
  • BDisable retries
  • CRetry instantly in a tight loop until it works
  • DIgnore the errors
Show the answer

Answer: A. Rate limits call for waiting and lower request rates.

S3An intermittent 529 overloaded response appears. What recovery fits?

  • AReduce temperature in case that helps the service
  • BRewrite the prompt in case it is too long
  • CRetry with exponential backoff and jitter, then fall back or queue
  • DTreat it as a permanent failure after one try
Show the answer

Answer: C. Overload is transient; backoff and fallback handle it.

S4Answers about deductibles are wrong for some policies. The logged prompt shows the policy text was truncated before it reached Claude. Where is the origin?

  • AThe user's browser, which sent the question in the wrong format
  • BThe integration layer that truncated the input, not the model
  • CThe API rate limit, which stopped some of the requests from running
  • DThe model's weights
Show the answer

Answer: B. The model never saw the needed text; fixing the data path fixes the answer.

S5Which TWO belong in a useful trace of each model call? Select TWO.

  • AOnly the user's name
  • BNothing, to protect privacy entirely
  • Cusage, stop_reason and latency
  • DThe request ID and the exact prompt, tool calls and results sent
  • EOnly the final answer text
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. End-to-end traces with identifiers, inputs, usage and stop reasons allow failure analysis (with sensitive data masked).

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
4xx Fix the request; do not retry unchanged
429 Back off, retry-after, lower concurrency
5xx / overloaded / timeout Retry with exponential backoff and jitter
max_tokens Cut-off output: raise limit or continue
Parsing Structured output, defensive parsing, retry with error
Wrong content Check what the model saw (prompt, context, tool data) first
Traces Request ID, prompt, tools, usage, stop_reason, latency (mask sensitive data)
Isolate Replay the exact request; integration layer vs model output
Evals Criteria first; task-specific with edge cases; automate; code, human or LLM grading; run on every change
